situation.person: Expecting and first-year parents in a Nigerian household with irregular income in the first 12 months, facing new baby costs while pay is paused or shrunk
situation.specific_situation: New recurring costs collide with shrunken income every month without a single trusted number, so every purchase is feared and every bill restarts the fight.
situation.trigger: Her salary stopped but the bills did not, and the hospital asked for a deposit before admission.
situation.problem: No first-year budget exists, therefore money disappears and the couple fights over baby spending.

evidence.claim: My salary stopped but the bills didn’t
Every week 5,000 naira disappears on diapers
Nigerian statutory maternity minimum: 12 weeks leave at no less than 50% wages with 6 months continuous service; nursing breaks 2x30 min; no statutory paternity leave.
evidence.source: Nigeria Labour Act s.54; ICLG Employment Guide Nigeria (updated 2026-03-20)

evidence.claim: Nigeria ranked last in first-year baby affordability: nappies/wipes/rash-cream ≈123.6% of average annual wage; formula ≈131.1%; figures dated June 2026 under an affordable-options methodology.
evidence.source: Remitly 2026 baby-affordability index via Guardian Nigeria (2026-09-10; re-verify before publishing use)

evidence.claim: Lagos 2026 tier-split birth ranges and 2026 retail formula listings are dated snapshots for mechanism calibration, not surveyed national prices.
